subject: Harmonizing invoice cadence + flexible ramp scenarios for renewal
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@statera.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: ops+procurement@statera.com, liz.moreno@statera.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Aligning renewal cadence + ramp smoothing questions

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the call this morning. Procurement asked me to follow up with a couple of concrete asks before we finalize terms:

1) Can Redwood align invoices to our fiscal quarter (Nov 1 start) rather than the current monthly cycle? If we co-term and move to an annual invoice, how will proration be handled for the partial first month?

2) On the ramp: our product team expects usage to ramp over 9 months rather than the 6 shown in the draft. Are you able to propose a flexible ramp schedule (9-month, stepped billing) and show the impact to unit pricing? We need scenarios for finance to approve.

Attaching the MA pricing workbook our CFO asked us to complete. Appreciate a short options packet we can take to legal/procurement.

Regards,
Samir Khan
VP, IT Ops — Statera Health
[attachment: Statera_MA_Pricing_Scenarios.xlsx (xlsx)]
From: kimberly.park@redwood.com <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@statera.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 16:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aligning renewal cadence + ramp smoothing questions

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the note and for sending the workbook. Quick answers up top:
- We can co-term to an annual Nov 1 start and invoice annually. First partial period will be prorated to the day; we typically compute a daily rate based on the annual committed units and invoice that partial period as a line item.
- We can do a 9-month stepped ramp. I pulled in a couple scenarios (9-month linear ramp, 3x-step ramp at months 1/4/7) and flagged how unit price and effective blended rate change.

Ive looped in Marissa (Renewals) for pricing alignment and Karthik (Rev Ops) to confirm invoicing mechanics. Ben, can you confirm how we present proration on the invoice and whether we can put separate invoice line items for committed vs overage during ramp?

Will circulate a short options PDF by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | kimberly.park@redwood.com
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, Samir Khan <samir.khan@statera.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aligning renewal cadence + ramp smoothing questions

Samir / Kimberly —

Attached is a concise pack with three scenarios:

A) Annual co-term (Nov 1) with 9-month linear ramp — daily prorate for initial partial period, single invoice annually (preferred for accounting simplicity).
B) Annual co-term with 9-month stepped ramp (25%/50%/100% effective committed bands at months 1/4/7) — invoiced annually with breakout line items for committed band and an overage summary retrievable in Console exports.
C) Hybrid: Quarterly invoices on Nov 1 co-term but annual commitment for pricing guarantees (prorated initial quarter) — useful if your treasury needs regular cashflow windows.

Key tradeoffs included on page 2: forecasting accuracy vs treasury/cashflow, and how the Console export maps to invoice granularity.

I included expected blended unit price and the % difference vs the 6-month ramp baseline. If you want any of these as a redline-ready amendment we can drop those numbers into a PO-ready table.

[attachment: 20260921-Redwood-FlexRamp-Term-Summary.pdf (pdf)]

Marissa Cole
Renewals Lead — Redwood Inference
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@statera.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, ops+procurement@statera.com
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aligning renewal cadence + ramp smoothing questions

Thanks — this is exactly what procurement asked for. A couple of follow-ups:

- Option B looks promising. Can you confirm if the stepped committed bands are enforced via the contract (committed units per band) or if they are guidance that could be exceeded and billed as overage? Procurement prefers committed + overage separation enforced in the SOW.

- For the hybrid option (C), how would credits work if we front-load a portion of the commitment? Would we do a credit schedule tied to the stepped ramp points?

If you can provide language snippets for the amendment (one paragraph per option), I can share with legal and get back with redlines. Also looped in our procurement alias for visibility.

—Samir
From: kimberly.park@redwood.com <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@statera.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 24 Sep 2026 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aligning renewal cadence + ramp smoothing questions

Samir —

Short answers and next steps:

- Commitment enforcement: Option B will be drafted with explicit committed unit bands in the amendment (SOW table). Overage invoices will be separate lines. Well add a clause that describes the measurement window for committed vs overage (monthly reconciliation with Console export).

- Hybrid credits: For Option C we propose a credit ledger that auto-applies to overage through month 9; credits are consumed in chronological order and expire at co-term. We can produce a sample credit schedule and a 1-page amendment paragraph for legal.

Next steps:
1) We will send a redline-ready amendment paragraph for Options B and C by Monday (Sep 27).
2) Karthik will confirm invoice line item naming conventions and a sample prorated invoice export.
3) If Statera is comfortable with wording we can initiate DocuSign for the SOW amendment and set the Nov 1 co-term effective date.

Kimberly Park
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
